sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Candidate faithfully encodes the verified direct-calculation requirement: it targets plating, validates QUDT quantity nodes with the declared units and positive operands, conditionally represents the exact 2 mm normal addition or a lower approved coated addition with required evidence, and applies the specified piecewise f2 formula with the required scaled tolerance and ratio bounds. Deterministic validation is valid and no canonical vocabulary repair is required.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the corrosion-addition alternatives: encode the exact normal value 2 mm with inclusive numeric bounds (sh:minInclusive 2 and sh:maxInclusive 2), not a SPARQL inequality filter, and constrain the approved coated branch to a genuinely lower value (< 2 mm), not FILTER (?addition >= 2.0). Keep the coated branch’s maintained-coating and evidenceState-approved constraints conditional on that lower-value branch. Also prevent the formula from evaluating at h/s = 0: require a strictly positive ratio (or strictly positive designIceLoadHeight together with spacing > 0) before calculating 0.4/(h/s). Preserve the supplied max(1e-6*ABS(expected),1e-12) tolerance and the plating owner/paths.

Deterministic validation prevents acceptance. Fix: Quantity property designIceLoadHeight must point to a QUDT QuantityValue node, not a direct literal datatype | Quantity property spacing must point to a QUDT QuantityValue node, not a direct literal datatype | Quantity property longitudinalPlatingFactorF2 must point to a QUDT QuantityValue node, not a direct literal datatype | Quantity property corrosionAbrasionAddition must point to a QUDT QuantityValue node, not a direct literal datatype | Quantity property corrosionAbrasionAddition must point to a QUDT QuantityValue node, not a direct literal datatype
Semantic validator feedback: Remove sh:datatype qudt:QuantityValue from every quantity property (designIceLoadHeight, spacing, longitudinalPlatingFactorF2, and both corrosionAbrasionAddition alternatives); these properties must point to QUDT QuantityValue nodes, so validate the nested node structure instead of declaring a datatype. Preserve the prior repairs: keep the normal corrosion addition at exactly 2 mm with inclusive bounds, keep the approved maintained-coating branch strictly below 2 mm and conditional on both specialSurfaceCoatingMaintained true and materialApprovalStatus approved, and prevent formula evaluation at non-positive h/s while retaining the specified max(1e-6*ABS(expected),1e-12) tolerance. Also explicitly constrain materialApprovalStatus to the canonical nltl:evidenceState range (for example with sh:class nltl:evidenceState) in the conditional branch.

Add an explicit constraint that the positive designIceLoadHeight-to-spacing ratio is no greater than 1.8. The current SPARQL query only evaluates and rejects mismatches when ?ratio <= 1.8, so any ratio above 1.8 produces no selected violation and can pass accidentally. Preserve the existing exact 2 mm inclusive branch, lower-than-2 mm approved maintained-coating branch with evidenceState approval, positive operands, owner/paths, and max(1e-6*ABS(expected),1e-12) tolerance.

Candidate faithfully encodes the verified direct-calculation requirement: it targets plating, validates QUDT quantity nodes with the declared units and positive operands, conditionally represents the exact 2 mm normal addition or a lower approved coated addition with required evidence, and applies the specified piecewise f2 formula with the required scaled tolerance and ratio bounds. Deterministic validation is valid and no canonical vocabulary repair is required.
